Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 8.pdf ---
BECS (Book E-Commerce System)
So basically what we're trying to do is get books selling 
online instead of however you guys are doing it now, just a 
simple site where people can come in, look through what's 
available, throw a few books in a cart and check out. Nothing 
crazy, I just want it to actually work and not be a headache 
to keep up with. Right now I think it's all kind of manual or 
scattered and there's no real way for someone to just browse 
and buy without someone in the middle handling it, so that's 
the itch we're trying to scratch here. 
 
Anybody coming to the site should be able to just make an 
account, that's it, no big verification process or anything, 
and once they're in they can search for books and see title, 
author, price, add stuff to their cart and go through 
checkout. Keep the search simple, just matching on the title 
and it has to be exact, nothing fancy like partial matches or 
letting people search by author, that's more than we need 
right now. Some of these people might want to sign up to get 
notified about promotions and deals, so let's call those folks 
members, and they're the ones who can use promo codes when 
they check out. I picture this being pretty bare-bones in 
terms of who can buy what, like one copy of each book per 
order is plenty, we don't need people stacking ten copies of 
the same thing in their cart. 
 
On my side of things, I need a way to manage the inventory, 
basically a login that lets me add new books, edit prices, see 
how much stock I've got, that kind of stuff. I also want the 
system to ping me, like an email or something, whenever a book 
is running low so I don't get caught without stock, unless 
I've told it not to bother for that particular book because 
maybe I'm discontinuing it. And I want to be able to set up 
these percentage-off promotions every now and then and have it 
just email all the members automatically when I create one. 
 
One thing I want to be upfront about, we don't need to 
actually process real credit cards or handle real money 
movement right now, just collect the card number as part of 
the checkout flow and spit out a receipt and keep a log of 
what was purchased, who bought it, when. The real payment 
processing piece is something for way later, not part of this. 
Same with security stuff, I know that sounds bad, but honestly 
for what we need right now I'm not worried about encryption or 
people forgetting passwords or whatever, that's not a 
priority, let's not spend time building password recovery or 
anything like that for now. 
 
There's only going to be one person managing the store, me 
basically, so don't worry about building out roles for 
multiple managers or anything fancy like that, and a manager 
should never also be a regular customer account, those are two 
separate hats. It just needs to run somewhere people can get 
to it through a normal browser, nothing exotic on the 
technical side, just something stable that people in here can 
pull up and use without issues.

Sistema: BECS (Book E-Commerce System)

Resumo executivo: BECS is a browser-based book e-commerce system that replaces manual or fragmented book-selling activities with customer self-service browsing, cart, checkout, receipt generation, purchase logging, inventory management, low-stock notifications, and member promotions. It enables customers to buy books without staff intervention while enabling the single store manager to maintain the catalogue, inventory, and promotions.

Escopo: The system enables customers to browse and order books online and enables one store manager to administer inventory and percentage-off promotions.
  Em escopo: Customer account registration and login
  Em escopo: Available-book browsing, exact-title search, book details, and shopping cart
  Em escopo: Checkout with card-number collection, receipt generation, and purchase logging
  Em escopo: Member promotion subscription and promo-code application
  Em escopo: Manager authentication, catalogue maintenance, stock visibility, and low-stock email alerts
  Em escopo: Percentage-off promotion creation and automatic member email notifications
  Fora de escopo: Real credit-card authorization, payment processing, and money movement — explicitly deferred to a later version
  Fora de escopo: Password recovery — explicitly excluded from this version
  Fora de escopo: Encryption and additional security features — explicitly not prioritized for this version
  Fora de escopo: Partial-title and author-based search — exact-title search only is required
  Fora de escopo: Multiple manager roles or manager-role administration — the store has one manager only
  Fora de escopo: Shipping, delivery, and order-fulfilment management — not specified in the scenario [INFERIDO]
  Premissa: PA-01: Customers and the manager have internet access and a supported web browser.
  Premissa: PA-02: An email delivery service is available for low-stock alerts and promotion notifications [INFERIDO].
  Premissa: PA-03: Customer account registration includes credentials required for subsequent login; the required registration fields are [TBD].
  Premissa: PA-04: Each low-stock-alert-enabled book has a manager-defined low-stock threshold; the default threshold is [TBD].
  Restrição: REST-01 (Platform): The system shall be accessible through a standard web browser.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Business): Only one manager account shall exist.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Scope): The checkout flow shall not process real payments.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Scope): Password recovery shall not be implemented.
  Restrição: REST-05 (Risk acceptance): Encryption and additional security controls are not part of this version, as explicitly stated in the scenario.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Customer (Primary user): Register an account, browse available books, search by exact title, manage a cart, complete checkout, and receive a receipt.
  STK-02 - Member (Primary user): Receive promotion notifications and apply promo codes during checkout.
  STK-03 - Store Manager (Primary user): Maintain books, prices, stock, low-stock alert settings, and promotions.
  STK-04 - Email Delivery Service (External stakeholder): Deliver low-stock alerts and promotion-notification emails [INFERIDO].

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Exact-title search: Books are searchable only by an exact match of their title.
  RN-002 - Member-only promo codes: Only members are eligible to use promo codes when placing an order.
  RN-003 - Single copy per book per order: An order may contain no more than one copy of each book.
  RN-004 - Low-stock alert eligibility: A book generates a low-stock notification when its stock reaches its configured low-stock threshold, unless alerts have been disabled for that book.
  RN-005 - Percentage-off promotion: Promotions reduce an eligible order amount by a configured percentage.
  RN-006 - No payment settlement: Orders are recorded without credit-card authorization, payment processing, or money movement.
  RN-007 - Single manager: The store has exactly one manager.
  RN-008 - Separate account roles: A manager account cannot also be a regular customer account.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Register customer account: The system shall register a customer account without an identity-verification process. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Authenticate customer: The system shall authenticate a registered customer before granting customer-area access. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Browse available books: The system shall display the catalogue of books available for purchase. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Search by exact title: The system shall return books whose title exactly matches the customer search term. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Display book details: The system shall display a selected book's title, author, and price. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Add book to cart: The system shall add a selected available book to the customer's cart. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Enforce single-copy limit: The system shall prevent a cart from containing more than one copy of the same book. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Collect card number: The system shall collect a card number as checkout input when a customer places an order. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Generate receipt: The system shall generate a receipt after a checkout is completed. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Log purchase: The system shall log the purchased items, purchasing customer, and order timestamp for each completed checkout. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Enroll as member: The system shall allow a registered customer to enroll as a member for promotion notifications. [Should have]
  RF-012 - Apply promo code: The system shall apply a valid promo code to an eligible member's checkout. [Should have]
  RF-013 - Authenticate manager: The system shall authenticate the manager before granting inventory or promotion-management access. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Add book: The system shall allow the manager to add a book to the catalogue. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Update book price: The system shall allow the manager to update a catalogue book's price. [Must have]
  RF-016 - View stock: The system shall display the current stock quantity for each catalogue book to the manager. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Send low-stock alert: The system shall send a low-stock email alert to the manager when an alert-enabled book reaches its configured threshold. [Should have]
  RF-018 - Configure low-stock alerts: The system shall allow the manager to enable or disable low-stock alerts for an individual book. [Should have]
  RF-019 - Create promotion: The system shall allow the manager to create a promotion with a percentage-off value and promo code. [Should have]
  RF-020 - Notify members of promotion: The system shall email every member when the manager creates a promotion. [Should have]
  RF-021 - Decrease stock after order: The system shall decrease the stock quantity of each purchased book after checkout completion. [Must have]
  RF-022 - Separate manager and customer accounts: The system shall reject assignment of both manager and customer roles to the same account. [Must have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Compatibility) - The system shall complete all supported customer and manager workflows with zero critical defects in the latest two major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. [TBD] | Métrica: 0 critical defects in the defined cross-browser regression suite for 8 browser-version combinations. [TBD]
  RNF-002 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall return catalogue browsing and exact-title search results within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 100 concurrent users. [TBD] | Métrica: 95th-percentile response time of 2 seconds or less under 100 concurrent users. [TBD]
  RNF-003 (Reliability) - The system shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.0%, excluding announced maintenance periods. [TBD] | Métrica: Maximum unplanned downtime of 7 hours and 12 minutes per 30-day month. [TBD]
  RNF-004 (Maintainability) - The system shall provide automated regression tests covering at least 80% of executable application statements to support maintenance. [TBD] | Métrica: Statement coverage of at least 80% in the continuous-integration coverage report. [TBD]

Histórias de usuário:
  HU-001 - Como customer, quero register an account, para access the online book store.
  HU-002 - Como registered customer, quero log in, para use my customer area.
  HU-003 - Como customer, quero browse available books, para find books to purchase.
  HU-004 - Como customer, quero search by an exact book title, para locate a specific book.
  HU-005 - Como customer, quero view a book's details, para decide whether to buy it.

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Register Customer Account | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer opens the registration page.
    2. The customer enters the required registration data.
    3. The customer submits the registration request.
    4. The system registers the customer account.
  UC-002 - Browse and Add Book to Cart | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer opens the available-book catalogue.
    2. The system displays available books.
    3. The customer selects a book.
    4. The system displays the book title, author, and price.
    5. The customer adds the book to the cart.
    6. The system adds one copy of the book to the cart.
  UC-003 - Complete Checkout | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer starts checkout.
    2. The system requests a card number.
    3. The customer enters a card number and confirms checkout.
    4. The system records the order without payment settlement.
    5. The system decreases stock for each purchased book.
    6. The system generates a receipt.
  UC-004 - Manage Inventory | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The manager opens inventory management.
    2. The system displays catalogue books and stock quantities.
    3. The manager adds a book or selects an existing book.
    4. The manager saves a new book, price update, or alert setting.
    5. The system saves the submitted inventory change.
  UC-005 - Create Promotion and Notify Members | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The manager opens promotion management.
    2. The manager enters a promo code and percentage-off value.
    3. The manager submits the promotion.
    4. The system creates the promotion.
    5. The system sends a promotion email to every member.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado a visitor is on the registration page, quando the visitor submits all required registration data, então the system creates one customer account without requesting identity verification
  CA-002 - Dado a registered customer provides valid credentials, quando the customer submits the login form, então the system grants customer-area access
  CA-003 - Dado at least one book is available for purchase, quando a customer opens the catalogue, então the system displays every available book
  CA-004 - Dado the catalogue contains books titled "Dune" and "Dune Messiah", quando a customer searches for "Dune", então the system returns "Dune" and does not return "Dune Messiah"
  CA-005 - Dado a book is displayed in the catalogue, quando a customer selects the book, então the system displays its title, author, and price
  CA-006 - Dado an available book is selected, quando the customer adds it to the cart, então the cart contains one copy of the selected book
  CA-007 - Dado the cart already contains one copy of a book, quando the customer attempts to add the same book again, então the cart still contains exactly one copy and the system displays a quantity-limit message
  CA-008 - Dado an authenticated customer has a non-empty cart, quando the customer submits checkout, então the system requires a card-number input before recording the order
  CA-009 - Dado checkout has completed, quando the order is recorded, então the system generates one receipt for the completed order
  CA-010 - Dado a customer completes checkout for one book, quando the order is recorded, então the purchase log contains the purchased book, customer identifier, and order timestamp
  CA-011 - Dado a registered customer is not a member, quando the customer enrolls for promotion notifications, então the system marks the customer as a member
  CA-012 - Dado a member has a valid promo code for a 10% promotion, quando the member applies the code at checkout, então the system reduces the eligible order amount by 10%
  CA-013 - Dado the manager provides valid manager credentials, quando the manager submits the login form, então the system grants access to inventory and promotion management
  CA-014 - Dado the manager is authenticated, quando the manager submits a new book, então the system adds the book to the catalogue
  CA-015 - Dado the manager is viewing an existing book, quando the manager saves a new price, então the system displays the saved price for that book
  CA-016 - Dado the manager is authenticated and a catalogue book has stock quantity 7, quando the manager opens inventory management, então the system displays stock quantity 7 for that book
  CA-017 - Dado a book has alerts enabled and a configured threshold of 2, quando its stock reaches 2, então the system sends one low-stock email alert to the manager
  CA-018 - Dado the manager is viewing a book with alerts enabled, quando the manager disables the alert setting, então the system saves the book's alert setting as disabled
  CA-019 - Dado the manager is authenticated, quando the manager submits promo code "SAVE10" with percentage-off value 10, então the system creates a promotion with code "SAVE10" and percentage-off value 10
  CA-020 - Dado three members exist, quando the manager creates a promotion, então the system sends one promotion email to each of the three members
  CA-021 - Dado a book has stock quantity 5 and is included in a completed checkout, quando the order is recorded, então the system updates the book stock quantity to 4
  CA-022 - Dado an account is assigned the manager role, quando an attempt is made to assign the customer role to the same account, então the system rejects the assignment and keeps the account assigned only as manager

Glossário:
  Available book: A catalogue book that is presented to customers for purchase.
  Customer: A person with a regular account who can browse and place book orders.
  Member: A registered customer enrolled to receive promotion notifications and eligible to use promo codes.
  Manager: The sole store-administration user, with an account that cannot also be a customer account.
  Promo code: A code associated with a percentage-off promotion and applicable only to an eligible member checkout.
  Low-stock threshold: The configured stock quantity at or below which an alert-enabled book triggers a manager email.
  Checkout: The process that records an order, collects a card number, decreases stock, and generates a receipt without processing payment.

Padrões, modelos e exemplos para elicitação e especificação de requisitos de software
conforme ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 · ISO/IEC 25010:2023 · SWEBOK v4.0 · BABOK® v3
Este documento é a base de conhecimento fixa (Vector Store B) do sistema de elicitação de requisitos. Ele ensina ao agente
de IA os padrões de escrita, templates, exemplos e regras de qualidade que devem ser aplicados ao analisar documentos 
de projeto.PARTE 1 — Estrutura do Documento de Especificação de Requisitos (SRS)
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

2023. A edição 2023 substituiu a de 2011 e acrescentou a característica Safety.
A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser 
classificado em uma dessas características. A seguir, cada característica com seus sub-atributos e 
exemplo de RNF.
1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 1. Functional Suitability
O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS 
vigente para o estado de destino, conforme tabela oficial CONFAZ, com variação máxima de R$ 0,01 em 
relação ao valor de referência da Receita Estadual.
2. Performance Efficiency (Eficiência de Desempenho)
 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 2. Performance Efficiency
O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com 
tempo de resposta inferior a 2 segundos no percentil 95.
3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 3. Compatibility
A API do sistema deve expor endpoints REST/JSON compatíveis com o padrão OpenAPI 3.0, permitindo 
integração com o ERP legado via OAuth 2.0 sem modificações no ERP.4. Interaction Capability (Capacidade de Interação) — antes 'Usabilidade'
 Appropriateness Recognisability — usuário reconhece a adequação do sistema.
 Learnability — facilidade de aprendizado.
 Operability — facilidade de operação.
 User Error Protection — proteção contra erros do usuário.
 User Engagement — interface envolvente e motivadora.
 Inclusivity — acessível a pessoas com diferentes capacidades.
 User Assistance — suporte ao usuário.
 Self-Descriptiveness — interface autoexplicativa.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 4. Interaction Capability
Um usuário sem treinamento prévio deve ser capaz de registrar seu primeiro pedido completo em até 10 
minutos. A interface deve seguir as diretrizes WCAG 2.1 nível AA.
5. Reliability (Confiabilidade)
 Faultlessness — ausência de falhas em condições normais.
 Availability — proporção de tempo em que o sistema está operacional.
 Fault Tolerance — operação correta mesmo com falhas parciais.
 Recoverability — recuperação após falha.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 5. Reliability
O sistema deve ter disponibilidade mínima de 99,5% ao mês (máx. 3,6h de downtime não planejado). Em 
caso de falha crítica, o sistema deve restaurar a operação normal em até 4 horas (RTO = 4h).

 Replaceability — substituível por outro produto equivalente.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 8. Flexibility
O sistema deve ser implantável em qualquer provedor de nuvem (AWS, GCP, Azure) utilizando contêineres 
Docker, sem necessidade de alterações no código-fonte ou nos arquivos de configuração de aplicação.
9. Safety (Segurança Funcional) — NOVO na edição 2023
 Operational Constraint — limita operação a intervalos seguros.
 Risk Identification — identifica riscos em tempo de execução.
 Fail Safe — modo seguro em caso de falha.
 Hazard Warning — alerta sobre condições perigosas.
 Safe Integration — integração segura com outros sistemas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 9. Safety
APLICÁVEL a sistemas críticos: saúde, industrial, financeiro, automotivo.
Em sistemas de monitoramento médico, o sistema deve entrar automaticamente em modo de alerta visual e 
sonoro quando a frequência cardíaca do paciente sair do intervalo [40, 180] bpm, sem latência superior a 
500ms.PARTE 4 — Regras de Qualidade e Checklist de Validação
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9 (atributos do requisito); IEEE 830-1998 §4 (atributos do bom SRS); Wiegers & Beatty 
(2013, cap. 11)
4.1 Palavras Proibidas em Requisitos
As palavras abaixo indicam requisitos ambíguos, subjetivos ou não verificáveis. Quando 
encontradas, o requisito deve ser reescrito com métricas objetivas.
• rápido / veloz / ágil: Substituir por: 'tempo de resposta inferior a X ms/s'
• fácil / simples / intuitivo: Substituir por: métrica de usabilidade (ex.: task completion em < N min)
• amigável / bonito / moderno: Atributo subjetivo — vai para diretrizes de UI, não para RF/RNF
• eficiente: Substituir por: consumo de CPU < X%, throughput > Y req/s
• seguro: Substituir por: característica específica da ISO 25010 Security com métrica
• geralmente / normalmente: Indica exceções não documentadas — especificar todas as condições
• etc. / e assim por diante: Indica incompletude — listar todos os itens explicitamente
• e/ou em um único requisito: Indica dois requisitos distintos — separar em dois IDs diferentes
• deve ser possível: Ambíguo — usar 'O sistema deve [ação específica]'
• pode / poderá: 'Pode' = opcional. Use 'deve' para obrigatoriedade
4.2 Convenções de Escrita
1. Use SEMPRE 'O sistema deve...' (verbo 'dever' no presente — indica obrigatoriedade). Em inglês:
'shall' = obrigatório; 'should' = desejável; 'may' = opcional.
2. Cada RF descreve UMA e apenas UMA funcionalidade. Se o texto contém 'e' ligando dois 
comportamentos distintos, divida em dois RFs com IDs diferentes.
3. Todo RF referencia o STK de origem. Isso garante rastreabilidade bidirecional.4. Toda RN usa IDs do tipo RN-NNN.

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present 
and future—understand what the system does.
Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn

Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

Propósito
O objetivo de Analisar o Estado Atual é compreender as razões pelas quais 
uma corporação precisa mudar algum aspecto de como ela funciona e o que

Descrição
Analisar o Estado Atual compreende a necessidade do negócio e como ela se

de base e contexto para a mudança.
Entradas
• Resultados de Elicitação: usado para definir e entender o estado atual.

corporação ou organização com frequência inicia um trabalho de análise 
de negócios para melhor entender essas necessidades.

desempenho, cultura, dependências, infraestrutura, influências externas 
da corporação e relações significativas entre estes elementos.

definida com base em um entendimento do estado atual.

If developers build exactly what 
customers initially request, they’ll probably have to build it again because customers often don’t 
know what they really need. In addition, the BAs might not be talking to the right people or asking 
the right questions.
The features that users present as their “wants” don’t necessarily equate to the functionality they 
need to perform their tasks with the new product. To gain a more accurate view of user needs, the 
business analyst must collect a wide range of user input, analyze and clarify it, and specify just what 
needs to be built to let users do their jobs. The BA has the lead responsibility for recording the new 
system’s necessary capabilities and properties and for communicating that information to other 
stakeholders. This is an iterative process that takes time. If you don’t invest the time to achieve this 
shared understanding—this common vision of the intended product—the certain outcomes are 
rework, missed deadlines, cost overruns, and customer dissatisfaction.
User classes
People often talk about “the user” for a software system as though all users belong to a monolithic 
group with similar characteristics and needs. In reality, most products of any size appeal to a diversity 
of users with different expectations and goals. Rather than thinking of “the user” in singular, spend 
some time identifying the multiple user classes and their roles and privileges for your product.
Classifying users
Chapter 2 described many of the types of stakeholders that a project might have. As shown in 
Figure 6-1, a user class is a subset of the product’s users, which is a subset of the product’s customers, 
which is a subset of its stakeholders. An individual can belong to multiple user classes. For example, 
an application’s administrator might also interact with it as an ordinary user at times. A product’s 
users might differ—among other ways—in the following respects, and you can group users into a 
number of distinct user classes based on these sorts of differences:
■ Their access privilege or security levels (such as ordinary user, guest user, administrator)
■ The tasks they perform during their business operations
■ The features they use
■ The frequency with which they use the product
■ Their application domain experience and computer systems expertise
■ The platforms they will be using (desktop PCs, laptop PCs, tablets, smartphones, specialized 
devices)CHAPTER 6 Finding the voice of the user 103
■ Their native language
■ Whether they will interact with the system directly or indirectly
FIGURE 6-1 A hierarchy of stakeholders, customers, users, and user classes.
It’s tempting to group users into classes based on their geographical location or the kind of 
company they work in. One company that creates software used in the banking industry initially 
considered distinguishing users based on whether they worked in a large commercial bank, a small 
commercial bank, a savings and loan institution, or a credit union. These distinctions really represent 
different market segments, though, not different user classes.
A better way to identify user classes is to think about the tasks that various users will perform with 
the system. All of those types of financial institutions will have tellers, employees who process loan 
applications, business bankers, and so forth. The individuals who perform such activities—whether 
they are job titles or simply roles—will have similar functional needs for the system across all of the 
financial institutions. Tellers all have to do more or less the same things, business bankers do more or 
less the same things, and so on. More logical user class names for a banking system therefore might 
include teller, loan officer, business banker, and branch manager. You might discover additional user 
classes by thinking of possible use cases, user stories, and process flows and who might perform them.

- Any visitor can create an account with no verification process.
- Logged-in users can search for books by title only, with an exact match (no partial matches, no search by author).
- Users can view a book's title, author, and price, add it to a cart, and check out.
- Only one copy of each book can be purchased per order.
- Members (a subset of registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
- The manager (a single login-based account) can add books, edit prices, and view stock levels.
- The system must automatically notify the manager by email when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that specific book.
- The manager can create percentage-off promotions; creating one automatically emails all members.
- The system does not process real credit card payments; it only collects a card number, produces a receipt, and logs the purchase (item, buyer, timestamp).
- Encryption and password recovery are explicitly out of scope for this version.
- There is only one manager account; no multi-manager roles are needed.
- A manager account must never also be a regular customer account.
- The system must run as a normal browser-accessible web application, with no exotic technical requirements.

em_escopo: Account creation for any visitor, with no verification process
Book search by exact title match (logged-in users)
Viewing book title, author, and price
Shopping cart with a limit of one copy per book per order
Checkout flow that collects a card number, generates a receipt, and logs the purchase
Member signup to receive promotion notifications and use promo codes at checkout
Manager login to manage inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock)
Automatic low-stock email alert to the manager, with per-book opt-out
Manager-created percentage-off promotions with automatic email to all members
fora_de_escopo: Real credit card / payment processing — deferred to a later phase
Encryption — not a priority for this version
Password recovery — not a priority for this version
Multiple manager accounts or manager roles — only one manager
Partial/fuzzy search or search by author — title search is exact-match only
Multiple copies of the same book per order — limited to one
premissas: PA-01: Only one person will operate the manager account for the store.
restricoes: REST-01 (Tecnica): The system must be usable through a normal web browser, with no exotic client-side requirements.

stakeholders.descricao: Store Manager — the single account responsible for managing inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock) and creating promotions; must never also be a regular customer account.
Visitor — anyone arriving at the site who can create an account with no verification process.
Registered User / Customer — logged-in user who can search for books, add them to a cart, and check out.
Member — a registered user who opted in to promotion notifications; the only type of user who can apply promo codes at checkout.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: A cart may contain at most one copy of each distinct book per order.
A manager account must never also function as a regular customer account.
Only members (not all registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
The low-stock email alert to the manager is suppressed for a given book if the manager has disabled notifications for that specific book.
Creating a new percentage-off promotion automatically triggers an email to all members.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow any visitor to create an account with no verification process.
The system must allow logged-in users to search for books by title using an exact match only (no partial match, no search by author).
The system must display each book's title, author, and price.
The system must allow users to add a book to their shopping cart.
The system must prevent a user from adding more than one copy of the same book to their cart in a single order.
The system must allow users to complete checkout for the items in their cart.
The system must allow a registered user to sign up as a member to receive promotion notifications.
The system must allow members to apply a promo code during checkout.
The system must provide a login for the manager, separate from customer accounts.
The system must allow the manager to add new books to the inventory.
The system must allow the manager to edit the price of existing books.
The system must allow the manager to view current stock levels.
The system must send an email notification to the manager when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that book.
The system must allow the manager to create percentage-off promotions.
The system must automatically email all members when a new promotion is created.
The system must collect a card number during checkout without processing an actual payment.
The system must generate a receipt after checkout.
The system must log each purchase, including the item, the buyer, and the timestamp.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must be usable through a standard web browser, with no exotic or non-standard client-side requirements.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a visitor, I want to create an account with no verification process, so that I can start using the site quickly.
As a registered user, I want to search for a book by its exact title, so that I can find the book I'm looking for.
As a registered user, I want to view a book's title, author, and price, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
As a registered user, I want to add a book to my cart, so that I can purchase it later.
As a registered user, I want to check out my cart, so that I can complete my purchase.
As a member, I want to apply a promo code at checkout, so that I can get a discount.
As the manager, I want to add new books and edit their prices, so that I can keep the catalog up to date.
As the manager, I want to be notified when a book's stock is low, so that I can restock in time.
As the manager, I want to create percentage-off promotions, so that I can attract more sales.
As a member, I want to receive an email when a new promotion is created, so that I know about current deals.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Search and Purchase Book — a logged-in user searches for a book by exact title, adds it to the cart, and completes checkout.
Manage Inventory — the manager logs in and adds new books, edits prices, or views current stock levels.
Create Promotion — the manager creates a percentage-off promotion, and the system automatically emails all members.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a logged-in user, when they search for a book title that exactly matches an existing book, then the system returns that book with its title, author, and price.
Given a user already has one copy of a book in their cart, when they try to add another copy of the same book, then the system prevents the second copy from being added.
Given a member is at checkout with a valid promo code, when they apply the code, then the system applies the corresponding discount.
Given a book's stock drops below the defined threshold and notifications are enabled for that book, when the stock update occurs, then the system sends an email to the manager.
Given the manager creates a new percentage-off promotion, when the promotion is saved, then the system automatically sends an email to all members.
